questions.question: Who was the Canaanite king who enslaved Israel in the days of Deborah?
questions.explanation: Sisera was the commander of his army. The oppression led to national paralysis: "the highways were deserted."

questions.question: True or false: Israel was enslaved to Jabin for twenty years.
questions.explanation: The people shut themselves in their settlements, the economy collapsed, and national morale was at a low.

questions.question: On what was Jabin's military power based?
questions.explanation: This was technology far superior to that of the tribes of Israel.

questions.question: True or false: Deborah sat under the "Palm of Deborah," between Ramah and Beth-el in the hill country of Ephraim.
questions.explanation: From there, in the heart of the land, she was an address for all the tribes who went up to her for judgment.

questions.question: According to "Tanna Devei Eliyahu," what did Deborah instruct her husband Lappidoth to do?
options: To go out to battle with Barak
To make thick wicks for the Tabernacle at Shiloh
To build an altar at Beth-el
questions.explanation: He was a simple man, and the wicks gave off much light, "lapidim," hence his name. Connection to the Lord also passes through practical service.

questions.question: What principle is learned from Deborah's prophecy, according to the Midrash?
options: Prophecy is passed down by inheritance
The Holy Spirit rests only in the Land of Israel
The Holy Spirit rests upon a person according to his deeds, whether man or woman
questions.explanation: At that time Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest was alive, and nevertheless Deborah prophesied, by virtue of her deeds and character.

questions.question: True or false: According to the Midrash, Deborah sat under a palm because its broad crown casts much shade.
questions.explanation: On the contrary: a palm has no broad crown, and so she sat in a visible place, to prevent "yichud" (seclusion) with those who came to her for judgment.

questions.question: To which mountain did Deborah tell Barak to draw the army?
questions.explanation: "Has not the Lord God of Israel commanded: Go and draw toward Mount Tabor?" Her prophecy was a practical military order.

questions.question: True or false: Barak son of Abinoam went out to war alone, without Deborah.
questions.explanation: Barak refused to go out without her presence, because he saw in her the conduit connecting to Divine Providence.

questions.question: What defeated the Canaanite chariotry, according to the research?
options: A night ambush on the mountain
Rain that flooded the Kishon and turned the valley into a swamp
The blocking of the water springs
questions.explanation: Chariots are effective on a plain but vulnerable in mud. Deborah ordered the descent from the mountain at the moment she knew through prophecy that rain had fallen.

questions.question: What did Deborah prophesy to Barak?
options: "The Lord will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman"
questions.explanation: The victory was completed in the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite.

questions.question: True or false: Barak killed Sisera on the battlefield.
questions.explanation: Jael killed him in her tent, and thus the prophecy "into the hand of a woman" was fulfilled.

questions.question: Which tribe did Deborah rebuke for remaining "among the sheepfolds to hear the whistling of the flocks"?
questions.explanation: Zebulun and Naphtali, by contrast, "risked their lives to the point of death." The song demands mutual responsibility from all parts of the nation.

questions.question: Against whom was the curse "because they came not to the help of the Lord" pronounced?
questions.explanation: One who refrains from helping his people in a time of distress is regarded as one who betrays his mission.

questions.question: How did Ben-Gurion and others interpret the epithet "a mother in Israel"?
options: A leader who cares for her people as a mother for her children
A woman who bore many children
The head of the tribe of Ephraim
questions.explanation: In contrast, the mother of Sisera is presented at the window, awaiting plunder and the subjugation of women.

questions.question: True or false: In her song, Deborah praised Zebulun and Naphtali.
questions.explanation: They enlisted for war and "risked their lives to the point of death on the heights of the field."

questions.question: How did the Tosafot explain that Israel went up to Deborah for judgment?
options: Because she was the daughter of a high priest
Because there were no male judges at that time
Perhaps they accepted her upon themselves voluntarily, because of the Divine Presence
questions.explanation: The public may accept upon itself someone who is not qualified by law, and then his rulings are binding. There are also those who saw in this a temporary ruling according to prophecy.

questions.question: How did Rabbi Uziel and Rabbi Herzog make use of the figure of Deborah?
options: As proof that women may not vote
As a source for the laws of inheritance
As proof that prophecy returns in our day
A democratic election is a "voluntary acceptance," and therefore women may serve in public positions
questions.explanation: Deborah thus became the halakhic precedent for women's partnership in the leadership of the nation.

questions.question: What does the palm under which she sat symbolize, according to the research?
options: Upright judgment without partiality, and one heart directed to heaven
The memory of the Exodus from Egypt
questions.explanation: "The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree": the palm is straight and tall, and like the lulav it has "one heart."

questions.question: According to one of the interpretations, who is "Lappidoth"?
options: Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest
Barak son of Abinoam, since "barak" (lightning) and "lapid" (torch) are both a sudden light
Heber the Kenite, the husband of Jael
questions.explanation: According to this, Deborah and Barak were a pair of leaders: the spirit and the practical force. Another interpretation sees in "wife of Lappidoth" a description of Deborah herself.
